content_voiceover: This slide covers NF1 diagnostic criteria and a Taiwan specific reimbursement update. For the diagnosis of NF1, a patient needs two or more of eight criteria, and this list is worth knowing cold for boards. First, a family history of NF1 in a first degree relative. Second, six or more café au lait macules, greater than zero point five centimeters before puberty or greater than one point five centimeters after puberty. Third, two or more neurofibromas or one plexiform neurofibroma. Fourth, freckling in the axillary or inguinal regions. Fifth, iris Lisch nodules, two or more, which are hamartomas that don't affect vision. Sixth, a distinctive bony lesion such as sphenoid dysplasia or long bone cortical thinning, which can present as bowing of the legs. Seventh, bilateral optic nerve gliomas, which rarely affect vision. And these criteria, taken together, two or more of the eight, establish the diagnosis, though formal confirmation should always come from a specialist. The bottom of the slide is a local practice note, in Taiwan, selumetinib, brand name Koselugo, became covered by National Health Insurance in February of twenty twenty five for patients aged three to eighteen with a confirmed diagnosis of neurofibromatosis type one who have inoperable, symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas, this reflects the same MEK inhibitor indication used internationally for progressive plexiform neurofibromas.
keypoints: NF1 diagnosis requires two or more of eight clinical criteria
Six or more café au lait macules is the most recognizable criterion
Lisch nodules are iris hamartomas that do not impair vision
Selumetinib, Koselugo, treats inoperable symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas in NF1
keypoint_voiceover: For NF1, know that diagnosis needs two of eight criteria, with café au lait macules, neurofibromas, axillary or inguinal freckling, Lisch nodules, optic glioma, and characteristic bone lesions being the classic exam list. Therapeutically, selumetinib is the MEK inhibitor now used for inoperable, symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas in NF1 patients.
